intro.zh:
你把新魔杖仔细收进衣袖，重新站回阳光斜照的鹅卵石街道。书页翻动、剪刀咔嗒、玻璃瓶碰撞和动物低鸣从四扇门后传来。

你可以点击商店，也可以直接输入想做的事。这里开始，按钮只是建议，而不是唯一的路。
intro.en:
You tuck your new wand safely into your sleeve and step back onto the sunlit cobbles. Turning pages, clicking scissors, chiming bottles, and animal calls spill from four open doors.

You may use the suggested actions or simply type what you want to do. From here on, buttons are suggestions—not the only path.

revisit.zh: 人流从你身边分开又合拢。四家商店仍亮着灯，已经买好的包裹在你手中轻轻碰撞。
revisit.en: The crowd parts and closes around you. Four shopfronts remain lit, and the parcels you have already bought knock softly together.

completion.zh:
最后一件物品被放进你的行李。羊皮纸清单上的墨迹自行连成一枚小小的星形印章：新生用品已经备齐。

对角巷仍可继续探索，而通往下一章的路也已经打开。
completion.en:
The final purchase settles into your luggage. Ink curls across your parchment list and forms a small star-shaped seal: first-year supplies complete.

Diagon Alley remains open to explore, and the road to the next chapter is ready.

intro.zh: 推门时，一摞过高的书摇晃着从你面前经过——下面只露出店员的一双鞋。空气里满是墨水、旧皮革与新羊皮纸的味道。
intro.en: As you enter, a dangerously tall stack of books walks past—only the clerk's shoes visible beneath it. The air smells of ink, old leather, and fresh parchment.

revisit.zh: 书架间仍有细碎的翻页声。一支羽毛笔追着写错价格的标签，在柜台上气急败坏地划线。
revisit.en: Pages continue to whisper between the shelves. A quill chases a mispriced label across the counter, crossing things out furiously.

greeting.zh: “一年级书单？我已经替你按课程顺序放好了。”
greeting.en: “First-year list? I have already arranged it in timetable order.”

warm_greeting.zh: “又见面了。你上次认真听我讲旧版课本的事，我给你留了纸张最好的一套。”
warm_greeting.en: “Back again. You listened to my old-edition story, so I saved the set with the finest paper for you.”

wary_greeting.zh: 他认出了你，只简短地点点头，把价签转向你的方向。
wary_greeting.en: He recognises you, offers only a brief nod, and turns the price label towards you.

talk.zh: 他压低声音告诉你：同一本教材的旧版批注有时比正文更有价值。说完，他在你的《魔法史》里夹了一张空白索引卡。
talk.en: He quietly tells you that notes in an old edition can be more valuable than the printed text, then slips a blank index card into your History of Magic volume.

followup.zh: “先读目录，再读脚注。迷路的时候，书会告诉你从哪一页重新开始。”
followup.en: “Read the contents first, then the footnotes. When you are lost, a book will tell you where to begin again.”

ignored.zh: 你没有回应。梅里索特先生停顿了一瞬，把那张原本准备送你的书签收回了抽屉。
ignored.en: You do not answer. Mr. Merrythought pauses, then returns the bookmark he meant to give you to its drawer.

label.zh: 购买一年级课本与羽毛笔
label.en: Buy first-year books and a quill

success.zh: 梅里索特先生用墨绿色纸绳捆好整套课本，又把一支新羽毛笔插在最上面。“别让它替你写作业——它会养成坏习惯。”
success.en: Mr. Merrythought ties the full set with dark-green cord and tucks a new quill beneath it. “Do not let it write your homework for you—it will develop bad habits.”

intro.zh: 卷尺像温顺的小蛇一样从衣架上滑下来，绕过你的肩、袖口和脚踝。几排深色长袍在镜子里显得比店里实际更多。
intro.en: Measuring tapes slip from their hooks like tame little snakes, circling your shoulders, sleeves, and ankles. Rows of dark robes multiply in the mirrors.

revisit.zh: 一只针线盒自动跳到工作台上，银针们整齐地转向你，像是在等待检阅。
revisit.en: A sewing box hops onto the worktable. Its silver needles turn towards you in a neat row, as if awaiting inspection.

greeting.zh: “站到矮凳上来，亲爱的。会长大的孩子，衣摆必须留一点聪明的余量。”
greeting.en: “Up on the stool, dear. Growing children need a clever little allowance in the hem.”

warm_greeting.zh: “回来得正好。我记得你的肩线——不用再量第二次。”
warm_greeting.en: “Perfect timing. I remember your shoulder line—no need to measure twice.”

wary_greeting.zh: 摩金夫人礼貌地笑了笑，卷尺却保持着职业性的距离。
wary_greeting.en: Madam Malkin smiles politely, though the measuring tape keeps a professional distance.

talk.zh: 她一边别住袖口一边告诉你，真正合身的长袍不会让人变得勇敢，却能让人忘记自己正在害怕。
talk.en: As she pins a sleeve, she says that a well-fitted robe cannot make someone brave, but it can help them forget they are afraid.

followup.zh: “口袋加固过了。学生总会往里面装比口袋更重的秘密。”
followup.en: “The pockets are reinforced. Students always put secrets in them heavier than the pockets were made to hold.”

ignored.zh: 你避开了她的问候。卷尺啪地缩回去，之后量尺寸时明显没有刚才那么温柔。
ignored.en: You pass over her greeting. The measuring tape snaps back and is noticeably less gentle when it resumes its work.

label.zh: 购买霍格沃茨校服长袍

success.zh: 最后一根线头自行缩进衣摆，长袍像一片安静的夜色落在你肩上。摩金夫人满意地抚平领口。
success.en: The final loose thread draws itself into the hem, and the robe settles over your shoulders like a quiet piece of night. Madam Malkin smooths the collar approvingly.

title.zh: 斯拉格与吉格斯药材店

intro.zh: 店里比街上凉得多。天花板垂下成束草药，玻璃罐里装着会缓慢呼吸的根茎；黄铜秤盘正独自校准分量。
intro.en: The shop is much cooler than the street. Bundles of herbs hang from the ceiling, roots breathe slowly inside glass jars, and brass scales calibrate themselves on the counter.

revisit.zh: 研钵仍在角落里规律地捣碎种子。苦涩、清凉和一点烧焦糖浆的气味分层停在空气中。
revisit.en: A mortar continues crushing seeds in the corner. Bitter, cooling, and faintly burnt-syrup scents hang in distinct layers in the air.

greeting.zh: “一年级套装在右边。别打开银色盖子的罐子，它比你好奇。”
greeting.en: “First-year kits are on the right. Do not open the silver-lidded jar—it is more curious than you are.”

warm_greeting.zh: “你回来了。很好，至少有人愿意先问标签是什么意思，再把东西倒进锅里。”
warm_greeting.en: “You came back. Good—someone willing to ask what a label means before tipping it into a cauldron.”

wary_greeting.zh: 艾夫斯先生把几只易碎瓶推远了一寸，才问你需要什么。
wary_greeting.en: Mr. Ives moves several fragile bottles an inch farther away before asking what you need.

talk.zh: 他教你用指节轻敲玻璃瓶：清脆声代表干燥，闷响则说明材料已经受潮。这可能会在第一堂魔药课救下一口坩埚。
talk.en: He teaches you to tap a phial with one knuckle: a clear note means dry ingredients; a dull one means damp. It may save a cauldron in your first Potions lesson.

followup.zh: “记住，冒烟不一定是失败。尖叫才通常是。”
followup.en: “Remember: smoke does not always mean failure. Screaming usually does.”

ignored.zh: 你径直越过他的提醒。一只银盖罐子在货架上轻轻碰了碰玻璃，像是记住了你。
ignored.en: You walk past his warning. A silver-lidded jar taps softly against the shelf, as though remembering you.

label.zh: 购买坩埚与魔药材料套装
label.en: Buy a cauldron and potion kit

success.zh: 艾夫斯先生逐一检查瓶塞，把材料按危险程度排进坩埚。“最麻烦的放最下面——这样你会记得别把包倒过来。”
success.en: Mr. Ives checks every stopper and nests the ingredients inside the cauldron by danger. “Worst ones at the bottom—so you remember not to turn the bag upside down.”

intro.zh: 门一开，各种声音立刻叠在一起：翅膀拍动、猫爪轻敲木板、蟾蜍低鸣，还有什么东西在后屋模仿收银铃。三双眼睛几乎同时望向你。
intro.en: The moment the door opens, sounds pile together: wings, cat paws on wood, a toad's low croak, and something in the back room imitating the till bell. Three pairs of eyes turn towards you at once.

revisit.zh: 动物们似乎比店主更早认出你。笼门、尾巴和一双鼓起的眼睛分别做出了自己的反应。
revisit.en: The animals seem to recognise you before the keeper does. A cage door, a tail, and a pair of round eyes each offer their own reaction.

greeting.zh: “别只看最漂亮的那只。先看看是谁一直在看你。”
greeting.en: “Do not choose only the prettiest one. First notice which animal has been watching you.”

warm_greeting.zh: “它们记得你的脚步声。看来你给大家留下了不错的第一印象。”
warm_greeting.en: “They remember your footsteps. It seems you made a good first impression.”

wary_greeting.zh: 瑞恩女士挡在最近的笼门前。“今天请慢一点。它们也会判断人。”
wary_greeting.en: Ms. Wren steps between you and the nearest cage. “Move slowly today. They judge people too.”

talk.zh: 她没有替你推荐，而是教你观察：猫头鹰先看方向，猫先看手，蟾蜍则要等四周安静后才会决定是否靠近。
talk.en: Rather than recommend one, she teaches you what to notice: an owl watches direction, a cat watches hands, and a toad waits for quiet before deciding whether to approach.

followup.zh: “伙伴不是装饰。你心情最糟的那天，才会知道彼此究竟选对了没有。”
followup.en: “A companion is not decoration. On your worst day, you will learn whether you truly chose each other.”

ignored.zh: 你没有理会她的话。那只原本向前挪动的动物停了下来，重新审视着你。
ignored.en: You disregard her advice. The animal that had edged closer stops and studies you again.

success.zh: 猫头鹰低下头，让你系好脚环，随后轻轻啄了一下你的手指——不疼，更像一份正式确认。
success.en: The owl lowers its head for the leg band, then taps your finger with its beak—not painfully, but like a formal confirmation.

success.zh: 猫从架子上跃下，绕着你的行李走了一圈，然后理所当然地坐在最上面。看来它已经替双方作出了决定。
success.en: The cat jumps down, circles your luggage once, and sits on top as if it belongs there. It appears to have decided for both of you.

success.zh: 蟾蜍安静地跳进软垫盒里，只在盖子合上前叫了一声。瑞恩女士说，那已经是它非常热烈的赞同。
success.en: The toad hops calmly into its padded carrier and croaks once before the lid closes. Ms. Wren says that counts as enthusiastic approval.
